modules.title: Module 1: Welcome & Mission
modules.description: Understanding LSC's mission, values, and community impact

content.text:
# What is LSC?

The L30 Library (LSC) is a community-centered library serving the fictional town of Somewhere Up North. We believe in making knowledge, resources, and community connection accessible to everyone.

## Our Core Values

- **Inclusivity** - Everyone belongs here
- **Access** - Free and open resources for the community
- **Community** - We build connections and support local culture
- **Growth** - We evolve with our community's needs
- **Integrity** - We're honest, transparent, and trustworthy

## What We Do

- Curate and maintain a diverse collection of books, media, and digital resources
- Host community events, workshops, and cultural programming
- Provide reference services and research support
- Create safe, welcoming spaces for learning and gathering
- Support local authors, artists, and creators

# LSC Community Impact

LSC isn't just about books—we're a pillar of community life in Somewhere Up North. Our impact includes:

- **150+ active patrons** using the catalog monthly
- **40+ events** hosted annually (book clubs, workshops, author talks)
- **Local partnerships** with schools, nonprofits, and businesses
- **Support for creators** - 30% of our collection features local authors
- **Accessibility** - 24/7 digital access, multiple learning formats, multilingual support

## Our Community Moments

- The annual Book Festival draws 200+ attendees
- Our "Reads & Coffee" series brings together 25-30 regulars weekly
- Teen programming serves 45+ young adults monthly
- Digital archive preserves local history and culture

# Your Role in LSC

Every staff member contributes to LSC's mission. Your role matters, whether you're curating collections, coordinating events, or supporting operations.

## General Staff Responsibilities

- Maintain welcoming, safe spaces
- Help patrons navigate resources
- Process materials and maintain collections
- Support event logistics

## Curator Responsibilities

- Evaluate and acquire new materials
- Organize and tag collections
- Manage digital metadata
- Recommend titles to patrons

## Event Coordinator Responsibilities

- Plan and promote events
- Coordinate logistics and vendors
- Manage registrations and communications
- Gather feedback and measure impact

modules.title: Module 2: Core Systems Basics
modules.description: Learning to navigate the LSC platform and complete daily workflows

content.text:
# Getting Around the Platform

LSC uses an integrated system to manage our catalog, events, and patron relationships. Here's what you need to know.

## Main Navigation

- **Home** - Overview of latest additions and featured content
- **Catalog** - Browse, search, and filter all materials
- **Events** - View, register for, and manage programming
- **Account** - Your profile, borrowing history, preferences
- **More** - Additional tools and resources

## Key Features

- **Search** - Find materials by title, author, subject, or keyword
- **Filters** - Narrow by type (book, ebook, video, etc.), format, language
- **Wishlist** - Save items for later borrowing
- **Notifications** - Get alerted when items are available or events start

# Basic Workflows

Most daily tasks follow simple workflows. Here are the ones you'll use most:

## Patron Inquiry Workflow

1. User searches the catalog
2. Staff member helps refine search
3. Material located and checked out or placed on hold
4. User notified when ready (if on hold)

## Event Registration Workflow

1. Patron browses events
2. Patron registers (online or in-person)
3. Confirmation sent
4. Reminders sent before event
5. Post-event feedback requested

## Administrative Workflow

1. Task created or assigned to you
2. You complete the task and mark as done
3. Task marked complete in system
4. Progress visible to the team

# Help & Resources

You're not alone! LSC has resources to help you succeed.

## Getting Help

- **Your Onboarding Buddy** - Assigned person for questions (first 2 weeks)
- **Staff Handbook** - PDF guide with policies and procedures
- **FAQ Section** - Common questions answered in the app
- **Team Slack** - Daily communication and quick questions
- **Weekly Team Meeting** - Thursdays 10am, discussion and planning

## Key Resources

- LSC Catalog Curation Guide (for curators)
- Event Planning Checklist (for coordinators)
- Accessibility Guidelines (everyone)
- Community Partnership List (reference)

modules.title: Module 3: Curator Deep Dive
modules.description: For team members curating our collection

content.text:
# Collection Curation Principles

As a curator, you're the gatekeeper of our collection quality and diversity.

## Selection Criteria

- Relevance to community interests and needs
- Author/creator diversity and representation
- Format appropriateness (print, digital, media)
- Condition and longevity
- Budget efficiency

## Our Collection Mix

- 60% Fiction (various genres)
- 20% Non-fiction (local history, practical skills, reference)
- 10% Young Adult & Children's
- 10% Media (documentaries, music, art collections)

## Diversity Goals

- 40% of new acquisitions from underrepresented authors/creators
- Materials in 8+ languages
- Accessibility formats (audiobooks, large print, braille)
- Local and indie publishers represented

# Metadata & Tagging

Good metadata makes materials discoverable. Here's how to tag effectively.

## Key Fields

- **Title & Author** - Exact as published
- **Genre/Category** - Use our standard taxonomy
- **Themes** - Multi-select tags (community, nature, history, etc.)
- **Language** - Mark all languages included
- **Accessibility** - Note audio, large print, digital formats
- **Local Connection** - Flag local authors, content about Somewhere Up North
- **Difficulty** - For educational materials (beginner, intermediate, advanced)

## Tagging Best Practices

- Be consistent with existing tags
- Use 3-5 descriptive tags per item
- Include themes that help discovery (not obvious ones)
- Mark accessibility formats prominently

# Acquisition Workflow

Here's how new materials get into LSC.

## The Process

1. **Identify** - Find potential acquisitions through vendors, recommendations, or community requests
2. **Evaluate** - Check criteria, budget, format, condition
3. **Propose** - Add to "Recommended" list with justification
4. **Approve** - Manager reviews and approves
5. **Purchase** - Order from vendor
6. **Receive** - Check quality and condition
7. **Process** - Add to catalog with metadata
8. **Shelve** - Place in collection

## Budget & Spending

- Track all spending in spreadsheet
- Report quarterly to manager
- Special requests require manager approval

modules.title: Module 4: Event Coordinator Deep Dive
modules.description: For team members coordinating LSC events

content.text:
# Event Types & Programming

LSC hosts diverse events that build community and celebrate learning.

## Recurring Events

- **Reads & Coffee** (Weekly, 20-30 attendees) - Book discussion, casual atmosphere
- **Teen Programming** (Monthly, 20+ teens) - Workshops, socials, book clubs
- **Author Talks** (Quarterly, 50-100 attendees) - Author readings and Q&A
- **Skill Workshops** (Monthly, 10-25 attendees) - Writing, tech, crafts, wellness

## Seasonal Events

- **Book Festival** (Annual, 200+ attendees) - Vendor fair, author signings, kids' activities
- **Local Creator Showcase** (Semi-annual) - Platform for local artists and writers
- **Summer Reading Program** (June-August) - Youth engagement with prizes

## Event Planning Basics

- Determine format (in-person, hybrid, virtual)
- Set date, time, capacity
- Plan logistics (space, materials, refreshments)
- Promote and register attendees
- Facilitate and gather feedback
- Follow up and document

# Event Logistics

Good logistics = great events. Here's the checklist.

## Before the Event (2-4 weeks out)

- Date/time confirmed
- Space reserved (in-person)
- Speakers/facilitators confirmed
- Marketing plan created
- Registrations open

## Week Before

- Confirm speaker/facilitator attendance
- Check tech setup (projectors, mics, internet)
- Prepare materials (handouts, name tags)
- Send reminder emails
- Brief team on roles

## Day Of

- Arrive early to set up
- Test all technology
- Welcome attendees warmly
- Facilitate program
- Take photos/document
- Collect feedback forms

## After the Event

- Thank speakers/volunteers
- Clean up and reset space
- Analyze feedback
- Document attendance/outcomes
- Share results with team
- Plan follow-ups

# Community Partnerships

LSC strengthens events through partnerships with local organizations.

## Current Partners

- Somewhere Up North Schools (student programs, book donations)
- Local nonprofits (co-hosted workshops, cross-promotion)
- Bookstores & publishers (author event coordination)
- Community centers (venue partnerships, audience reach)
- Media (coverage and promotion)

## Building Partnerships

- Identify shared mission/values
- Start with a conversation (coffee meeting)
- Propose win-win collaboration (both benefit)
- Document agreement (basic MOU or email)
- Execute event together
- Evaluate and debrief
- Plan next steps

quiz_questions.explanation: 'Reads & Coffee' is a weekly event that brings together 25-30 regulars.

quiz_questions.explanation: It's best practice to confirm speakers 2-4 weeks before the event.

modules.title: Module 5: General Staff Deep Dive
modules.description: For all staff members supporting LSC operations

content.text:
# Patron Service Excellence

You're the face of LSC. How you interact with patrons shapes their experience.

## Service Principles

- **Greet everyone warmly** - Even when busy, acknowledge people
- **Listen actively** - Understand what they really need
- **Help proactively** - Don't wait for them to ask
- **Be patient** - People have different needs and paces
- **Follow up** - Remember people and their preferences

## Common Scenarios

### Patron can't find a book

1. Search the system together
2. Check shelves in-person
3. Explain why it might not be available
4. Offer alternatives: place hold, similar titles, search again later

### Patron wants a recommendation

1. Ask what they enjoy (genre, recent reads, themes)
2. Suggest 2-3 titles with brief descriptions
3. If unsure, offer to research and get back to them
4. Write down their email/contact

### Patron has a complaint

1. Listen without interrupting
2. Empathize ("I understand that's frustrating")
3. Explain what happened (if you know)
4. Offer solutions
5. Escalate to manager if needed

# Collection Maintenance

Keeping our collection in great shape is everyone's job.

## Daily Tasks

- Straighten shelves and face books outward
- Remove damaged books (send to processing)
- Organize holds shelf
- Process returned items
- Check for items out of place

## Item Condition Assessment

- **Good** - No damage, readable, clean
- **Worn** - Normal wear, still usable
- **Damaged** - Missing pages, water damage, broken binding
- **Unsalvageable** - Beyond repair

## When to Remove Items

- Not used in 2+ years (check circulation data)
- Damaged beyond repair
- Outdated information (especially reference materials)
- Duplicate excess copies
- Community request for removal

modules.title: Module 6: Your First Week
modules.description: Getting started and integrating into the LSC team

content.text:
# Your First Week Checklist

Your first week sets the tone. Here's what you need to do:

## Day 1: Orientation

- Meet your onboarding buddy
- Tour the physical space (library, offices, breaks areas, restrooms)
- Get your account credentials and access
- Review emergency procedures
- Introduction to staff team
- **Time: 2-3 hours**

## Day 2-3: System Training

- Complete online orientation
- Practice logging in and basic navigation
- Learn your department's key tools
- Shadow a team member for 2+ hours
- **Time: 4-6 hours total**

## Day 4: Role-Specific Training

- Deep dive into your specific role
- Review procedures and workflows
- Ask questions and take notes
- Get overview of current projects
- **Time: 3-4 hours**

## Day 5: Integration

- Attend team meeting
- Meet with your manager (30-min check-in)
- Identify your first task or project
- Build relationships with teammates
- Reflect on your week
- **Time: 3-4 hours**

## First Week Goals

- Feel welcomed and oriented
- Understand your role and responsibilities
- Know where to find resources and ask for help
- Connect with at least 3 team members
- Complete your first task or project successfully
- Schedule 1:1 with manager for next week
